roles.title: Parties reviewer
roles.mirrors: defense counsel mapping parties and contractor tiers from the records
roles.brief: You are the parties reviewer on a construction claim. You work out, from the records only, who the parties are, what role each had on the project, and how they are related: who contracted with whom, who represented whom, who reviewed whose submittals, who supplied what, who inspected.
roles.default_focus: every organisation and person named, their roles, the relationships between them, and names written differently for the same party
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

roles.title: Technical reviewer
roles.brief: You are the technical reviewer on a construction claim. You record, from the records only, the design requirements, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests and their results, deviations from requirements, and when each happened. You state facts, never causes.
roles.default_focus: dated events: design requirements and values, submittals and approvals, tests and results, problems reported, repairs, and what the documents do not contain
roles.sees: the documents it is assigned, in full

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites, after collapsing whitespace and folding curly quotes and dashes. Case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled) is refused.
A quote on a page outside the readable claim file is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document, with its source span.
An event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.
A party's name must appear in its quotes; a relationship's two parties must both appear in its quotes.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A claim with no citation is shown as interpretation, never as fact.
One failed citation refuses the whole claim. Refused claims are kept with their reasons, not softened.
harness.negative_rule: Each role proposes what the claim file does not contain at the end of the run, with search terms that would find a counter-example. A negative is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory_collections.pages / documents / metadata: the ingested claim file, written only by ingestion
memory_collections.coverage: every read and search, with the pages it covered
memory_collections.refusals: refused claims with the verifier's reasons
memory_collections.workers: every reader started: role, documents, focus, tokens
memory_collections.trace: one event per step of the run
memory_collections.checkpoints: LangGraph run state, so a run can stop and resume
memory_collections.outputs: chronology, party map, exhibits and coverage report
memory_collections.cache: Reducto and Gemini responses, so nothing is paid for twice

chronology.statement: MassHighway hired the joint venture of Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff to manage design, construction, and day-to-day administration of the CA/T Project.
B/PB prepared a Preliminary Design Report for the tunnel finish design requiring the contractor to determine reinforcing bar locations prior to drilling.
Powers Fasteners adapted product literature regarding the Callahan Tunnel suspended ceiling anchor installation from a newsletter article.
Project staff conducted a claims avoidance review of the tunnel finishes contract specifications and noted the testing protocol lacked remedies for failed bolts or spot-checking provisions.
MassHighway awarded the C05B1 tunnel finishes contract to Walsh Construction of Illinois.
Prior to installing anchor bolts in April 1994, the contractor submitted Request for Information No. 126 to B/PB requesting reconsideration of the specification to use water to clean the holes.
Testing of anchor bolts began, with eight of the first 50 bolts failing.
The Project issued Deficiency Report No. 45 to the contractor on August 8, 1994.
The contractor requested permission to drill through rebar after rebar interference began delaying ceiling installation.

answer_key.summary: Powers reports torque of 120 ft-lb (above the 50-90 ft-lb range), says adhesive problems show up immediately in testing rather than over time, and recommends proof load testing; it does not identify creep.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: In an October 29, 1999, letter to Modern Continental, Powers documented the findings of the company’s examination of the displaced anchors.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental rejects improper installation or erection as the cause, says it will remove and replace the moved anchors per Powers, and reserves a claim because the root cause is undetermined.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On November 8, 1999, Modern Continental wrote to B/PB and included the Powers letter as an attachment.

answer_key.summary: B/PB disputes that the ceiling was installed per contract (over-torqued anchors, non-uniform hanger loads), concurs with removal and replacement, reconfirms the design loads and denies the claim.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: B/PB acknowledged receipt of this correspondence in a November 11, 1999, letter to Modern Continental.

answer_key.summary: Retested at the standard 3.25-kip load, the most displaced mock-up anchor (9/16 inch) pulls out with almost no resistance; the field architect attributes it to insufficient epoxy, dust and poor mixing and notes it slipped after weeks of constant load.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: According to the B/PB engineer daily report, on November 12, 1999, Conam representatives performed a proof-load test on the HOV anchor that had shown the most displacement (9/16 inch).

answer_key.summary: B/PB and Modern Continental check torque on randomly selected anchors (66 in WB on 9 Nov, 64 in EB on 15 Nov) and find it within the manufacturer's range.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Field reports for November 9 and November 15, 1999, documented tests performed by B/PB and Modern Continental engineers to verify the torque values of adhesive anchors in the D Street portal

answer_key.summary: Ironworkers hang five ceiling modules in the eastbound bore (NTSB places the accident module among the five installed that day).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: According to the field engineer daily report, the ceiling module involved in this accident was one of five modules installed on November 17, 1999.

answer_key.summary: Powers sends Modern Continental a repair procedure for the moved anchors: remove, clean the hole, reinstall with new rod and proof load per job specifications.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Modern Continental proposed to address the deficiency by following procedures recommended by Powers in a November 30, 1999, submittal to the contractor.

answer_key.summary: B/PB issues Deficiency Report No. 001: at least five ceiling adhesive anchors in module HOV 079 have pulled out since the module was hung.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On December 1, 1999, B/PB issued Deficiency Report 001 regarding the failed anchors.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental responds to DR-001 that the Powers site visit could not determine the cause of failure and proposes the Powers repair procedure.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Modern Continental responded to the deficiency report on December 2, 1999, detailing the actions the company was taking to resolve the issue.

answer_key.summary: Sigma Engineering's structural calculations for the fourth anchor adequacy submittal (723.480-014 C) compare design service loads with the manufacturer's allowable of 6,350 lb, without naming an epoxy formulation.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On December 17, 1999, the anchor capacity structural calculations were certified by a registered professional engineer employed by Sigma Engineering International, Inc., of Lincoln, Rhode Island.

answer_key.summary: Submittal 723.480-014 C includes Powers' draft reissue of ICBO ER-4514 (dated 1 Oct 1999), which permits Standard Set for long-term dead and live loads but limits Fast Set to short-term wind or earthquake loads.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The draft report revision limited the use of the Power-Fast Fast Set epoxy to “short term loads such as those resulting from wind or earthquake forces.”

answer_key.summary: B/PB rejects the DR-001 fix as submitted (submittal 723.480-016 A, returned 27 Dec), asks for the epoxy manufacturer and type used by Powers, and directs proof tests of 7,900 lb with all other anchors in question.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On December 27, 1999, B/PB returned the submittal to Modern Continental, rejecting the proposed response to Deficiency Report 001.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental objects that the 7,900-lb retest is inconsistent with the 3,250-lb contract requirement and asks for a modification (CP-022).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: In subsequent correspondence, the 7,900-pound proof test load was reduced to 6,350 (the calculated allowable load for the anchor), but the issue remained as to who would pay for the retesting of the previously installed anchors.

answer_key.summary: Gannett Fleming and B/PB return submittal 723.480-014 C with work allowed to proceed, asking only for the final ER-4514 when issued.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On January 7, 2000, Gannett Fleming authorized the contractor to proceed with the anchor installation (which had been underway since the previous July) pending final approval of the anchors.

answer_key.summary: B/PB states the removed anchor was improperly installed and over-torqued, sets 6,350 lb as the allowable bond strength, and requires retesting (DR-001 corrective action).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: B/PB, in a January 7, 2000, letter to Modern Continental, stated

answer_key.summary: Gannett Fleming approves anchor submittal 723.480-008 D (seal-plug installation procedure) as Work May Proceed Subject to Changes, asking for the final ER-4514; no formulation is identified.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: On February 4, 2000, Gannett Fleming (with secondary review by B/PB) approved Modern Continental’s anchor submittal, thus authorizing use of the anchoring system that had been installed in the failure area in late summer 1999.

answer_key.summary: Modern Continental's revised repair procedure (723.480-016 B) adopts proof testing of replacement anchors at 6,350 lb in the HOV mock-up, following B/PB's 7 January 2000 direction.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: In February, the management consultant and the contractor reached an agreement under which all the failed anchors would be replaced in accordance with the approved procedures and proof tested to 6,350 pounds.

answer_key.summary: A B/PB field engineer recommends closing DR-001: 19 of 187 HOV anchors failed the 6,350-lb retest, attributed to the installation learning curve.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Modern Continental retested a total of 187 anchors in the HOV area and experienced 19 failures.

answer_key.summary: B/PB closes Deficiency Report No. 1 after verifying that all HOV anchors were retested and failures replaced; no further monitoring is required.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The corrective actions taken by Modern Continental were verified by B/PB in late 2000, and Deficiency Report 001 was closed on January 26, 2001.

answer_key.summary: Contract Modification 158FW pays Modern Continental for retesting the HOV ceiling anchors at 6,350 lb, splitting the cost of anchors that passed 3,250 but failed 6,350.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The CA/T project agreed to pay the testing cost for any anchor that

answer_key.summary: ICBO Evaluation Service reissues ER-4514 in final form. Like the October 1999 draft, it permits Power-Fast Fast Set with threaded rod only for short-term (wind or earthquake) loads and reduces Fast Set bond strength by 25 percent (safety factor 5.33 instead of 4).
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The final version of the reissued ICBO ER-4514 was dated February 2000.

answer_key.summary: B/PB submits the Inspection Manual for Tunnels and Boat Structures to the MTA. The manual is not put into use before the collapse, and the pilot inspections the MTA began arranging in late 2005 are never carried out.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Investigators asked MTA officials why the inspection manual was not used from the time it was published in November 2003 until the day of the ceiling collapse.

answer_key.summary: About 11 p.m., the M1 row of anchors in eastbound ceiling module EB081 pulls out. The suspended concrete ceiling swings down onto a passing car, and the passenger is killed.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: As the car approached the end of the I-90 connector tunnel, a section of the tunnel’s suspended concrete ceiling detached from the tunnel roof and fell onto the vehicle.

answer_key.summary: During on-scene work, investigators measure every anchor left in the portal roof. Many have displaced downward, and the displaced share is greatest in the most heavily loaded rows.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: After the accident, 161 of the 634 remaining adhesive anchors supporting the D Street portal ceiling were found to have measurable displacement,

answer_key.summary: The NTSB Materials Laboratory examines the 20 failed M1-row anchors and others from the tunnel. Yellowed epoxy appears only on anchors that had displaced (0.5 inch or more), and on one failed anchor it reaches about 4 inches up the embedment.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: 13 of the 20 anchors in that row showed a yellow discoloration found only on displaced anchors.

answer_key.summary: MIT's FTIR analysis for the NTSB matches all epoxy samples from the tunnel to Powers Fast Set, not Standard Set. An FHWA report states that construction invoices also show a fast-set formula was used.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy at MIT showed that all of the samples from the tunnels, including the samples from the accident site, matched to the Fast Set reference samples.

answer_key.summary: The FHWA runs sustained-load (creep) tests on anchors still installed in the westbound portal roof. In 3 of the 9 rigorous tests the displacement never stabilizes; two anchors pull out completely.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: During the sustained load tests, two anchors pulled completely free of the tunnel roof.

answer_key.summary: In 82-day FHWA laboratory creep tests, anchors set with Power-Fast Fast Set creep at every load, and those loaded to 4,000 lb fail. Standard Set anchors barely move under the same conditions.
answer_key.ntsb_quote: The testing showed that anchors installed with the Powers Fast Set epoxy, using best practices, exhibited significant and continued displacement (creep) when subjected to loads as low as 1,000 pounds.

events.summary: 172 documents in the claim file
Outdated equipment product literature unrelated to adhesive anchor system design or installation.
Standard transmittal cover sheets conveying no substantive technical findings or contractual terms.

Analyze the mechanical failure mechanism of the suspended ceiling anchor system, evaluate the long-term creep and tensile performance of the specified and installed adhesive compounds, assess pullout test data and deficiency reports, and determine whether installation procedures adhered to engineering standards and manufacturer specifications.

Establish the contractual framework, division of responsibilities, submittal and approval history for the adhesive anchor system among Modern Continental, Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff, and Powers Fasteners, and verify whether timely notice of claims and non-conformance was provided in accordance with contract terms.

The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (MTA) acted as the project authority representing the Massachusetts Highway Department (par-79fda5cf540e, rel-85d4c86b75bc). Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) served as the project management consultant and engineer overseeing general contractor Modern Continental Construction Co., Inc. (MCC) and reviewing its submittals (par-9e21da513474, par-a4dd810e276b, rel-16076210a380, rel-9e358de424fa). Powers Fasteners, Inc. supplied adhesive anchors to MCC (par-a89aefe527c8, rel-c2a0fb871269), while SIGMA Engineering provided structural calculations for MCC (rel-fdd833e79975) and Conam Inspection conducted anchor tension testing for MCC (rel-9632e76195f2). Adhesive ceiling anchorage installation and testing procedures were set by Addendum No. 12 to Specification Section 723.480 (eve-9f5aadd4ca0b). After anchor displacement was identified in the HOV ceiling mockup in September and October 1999 (eve-37835b5e0d7f, eve-83bf893053c1), B/PB directed MCC to investigate with the manufacturer and abandon or replace moving anchors (eve-21836dcf40c6). Powers Fasteners provided technical repair recommendations (eve-1d798f59998c, eve-47b2aba7e268), but B/PB rejected initial repair Submittal 723.480.016 A on November 30, 1999 (eve-9dd975510fd0) and issued Deficiency Report No. 001 (DR-001) on December 1, 1999 (eve-591f6af5d07f). MCC's subsequent repair procedure Submittal No. 723.480-016 B was submitted January 28, 2000 (eve-b440fe5603a1) and approved subject to indicated changes on February 16, 2000 (eve-468958a8d701). Following completion of re-testing and anchor replacements, B/PB closed DR-001 on January 26, 2001 (eve-b72a98d5b81e, eve-14a38b32b57b), and MTA authorized Field Work Order Modification No. 158FW for the testing work on March 14, 2001 (eve-9a0e72d0a606, eve-d6d349f81c34).
Review project correspondence, meeting minutes, daily logs, agency communications, and investigative interview transcripts regarding anchor selection, approvals, and contractual relationships.

Analyze structural drawings, anchor specifications, adhesive manufacturer technical literature, tensile/proof load test reports, and technical failure analysis reports by NTSB, FHWA, and NIST regarding creep and adhesive anchor failure mechanisms.

Project records document that during initial testing under contract C05B1 in June 1994, eight of the first 50 anchor bolts failed [eve-5dbad4878292], following a May 1992 claims avoidance review noting the testing protocol lacked remedies for failed bolts [eve-00dd3bf65de0]. Deficiency Report No. 45 was issued on August 8, 1994 [eve-9e44ff517ceb], and a December 1994 field engineer report documented five failures among 58 tested anchors [eve-18a91d7589a1]. In January 1995, Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff approved core-drilling through reinforcing steel to install ceiling anchors [eve-5a4fd85669c7], which was subsequently reviewed in a December 1998 Inspector General report [eve-bc1984c93613, eve-5849700bc253]. On October 8, 1999, gap pull-out measurements between the tunnel roof and ceiling hanger plates were recorded in the HOV mock-up ceiling [eve-873453e0f68a]. In early 2000, Submittal No. 723.480-008 D for adhesive anchoring systems and Submittal No. 723.480-016 B for anchor repair procedures were approved subject to indicated changes [eve-cc8fb794219e, eve-7843b3dacb6e, eve-afd4a5f8597c, eve-72d8b65fff35, eve-6a1e775ea897]. Pullout testing by Conam Inspection between July and August 2000 identified failures along Lines A, B, and C, with specific locations failing initial tests and re-tests before passing subsequent retests [eve-d4941f6ff2b8, eve-359e42d8b66a, eve-fa8fdf9ff180, eve-879ae5f082e3, eve-f09e88603ff6].
Review general and contract-related records for project governance, contractual responsibilities, and procedural communications.
Analyze anchor testing data, laboratory inspection results, manufacturer product specifications, engineering procedures, and structural drawings.

Project records identify the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority acting on behalf of the Massachusetts Highway Department as project owner, with Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff serving as the management consultant and engineer of record (rel-85d4c86b75bc, par-fa39a53eae72). Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff oversaw general contractor Modern Continental Construction and Section Design Consultant Gannett Fleming, reviewing submittals alongside Gannett Fleming (rel-16076210a380, rel-bd21a9b0c49b, rel-9e358de424fa, rel-e4443effbacc). Powers Fasteners supplied the adhesive anchors to Modern Continental, with CEL Consulting inspecting for Powers Fasteners and Conam Inspection performing testing and inspections for Modern Continental (rel-c2a0fb871269, rel-d28c78337748, rel-9632e76195f2). Anchor installation began in June 1999 following design coordination meetings between Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff and Gannett Fleming regarding adhesive transfer load criteria, with Hilti providing technical drilling assistance (eve-e4a2e6730a26, eve-6a2252a26055, eve-b33dbb048ab2).

Review Powers product literature and technical specifications regarding adhesive anchor formulations, creep performance, load capacities, and installation instructions, alongside the NIST report findings concerning adhesive anchor performance and failure mechanisms.

Project records identify MassHighway as the project oversight and owner agency [par-6a2713630e37, par-e0ea2bb86f5c], with Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff acting as management consultant and construction manager [rel-e5c16593a433, par-0dd37fa6a5e7], Domenech Hicks Krockmalnic as section design consultant [par-21f6e9579d7e], and Walsh Construction of Illinois as construction contractor [rel-f7787f98dd01, par-aae92961cb20]. Ceiling support system revisions and installation procedures were prepared by EST/HNTB [par-6eb09d28fd2e], while Modern Continental Construction contracted with Conam Inspection [rel-e5a39491f5d6, par-93ffca5a8a9c] and Gannett & Fleming performed submittal reviews [rel-07f6df84ed6f, par-58894ff92fb3]. Fasteners and adhesive products were manufactured and supplied by Powers Fasteners and Sika Corporation [par-2a4d13819621, par-3595801462f1, par-6a51aba71def, par-91000f7f6067]. Investigation, physical examination, displacement measurements, and material testing were performed by the Federal Highway Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board Materials Laboratory, along with contracted laboratories including Standard Testing and Engineering Company, Bodycote Polymer – Broutman Laboratory, and Trace Laboratories-East [par-ca91037e92aa, par-5c995d9b1036, par-1d0bded7ed28, par-f425c69e6f91, rel-490b01df5a71, rel-1fccab542ce0, rel-27a86bd58a37].

Project governance records establish that the Massachusetts Turnpike Authority acted on behalf of the Massachusetts Highway Department as the project authority (rel-85d4c86b75bc, par-faedb15de8b2, par-79fda5cf540e). Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) served as the Management Consultant and project manager, overseeing general contractor Modern Continental Construction (MCC) (rel-16076210a380, par-bb6212e03911, par-4d44755460ba), with Robert E. Steffy acting as Resident Engineer representing B/PB and the Project Director (rel-b8d94e45a179, rel-1bd965fe7bcf). Gannett Fleming served as the Section Design Consultant under B/PB oversight (par-9fbe813f1068, rel-bd21a9b0c49b). Both B/PB and Gannett Fleming performed submittal reviews for MCC (rel-9e358de424fa, rel-e4443effbacc). Within MCC's tier, SIGMA Engineering provided structural design calculations (rel-fdd833e79975), Powers Fasteners supplied adhesive anchors (par-74bc8ad62126, rel-386abe252628), Environmental Interiors was contracted for ceiling and wall components (par-d5ad2738e37d, rel-33ec828334bc), and Conam Inspection performed testing and inspection services (par-a292dc4996d5, rel-9632e76195f2). Specialty subcontractors under MCC included Norfolk Mechanical, Patent Construction Services, and Cohn (rel-af74f69f98f7, rel-89cb0130575a, rel-b123a7ed87eb). Procedural records document technical coordination between Gannett Fleming and B/PB regarding anchor design criteria and specifications (eve-365ae25348ff, eve-e4a2e6730a26, eve-fb66c0f20ad7), B/PB's review and rejection of MCC's Value Engineering Cost Proposal No. 1 (eve-f59b3bac4fc6, eve-0d2f1eb3375c, eve-104f7fe2b706), and field installation oversight involving Hilti technical support for anchor drilling operations (eve-6a2252a26055, eve-b33dbb048ab2, rel-ab15008dfcb9).

The technical record documents that Powers Fasteners, Inc. served as the anchor and fastener manufacturer and supplier [par-572ab953b404, par-3595801462f1, par-d835e1eebad4], with Sika Corporation identified as the adhesive formulator, manufacturer, and supplier [par-492115b608d0, par-6a51aba71def, par-1d0ac17d3a67]. CEL Consulting performed quality control inspections for Powers Fasteners, Inc. [rel-111b103162f3, par-01aeda938f55], and evaluation reporting involved ICBO Evaluation Service, Inc. [par-3785dbb44726, par-bddfa7834f8f]. Investigative testing and evaluation of the adhesive anchors were conducted by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) by researchers Aaron Forster, Donald Hunston, and Joannie Chin [par-89446cbd4d41, par-522accc78137, par-64dcd3b732b0, par-554089d5f333, par-59c9a631ab9f], alongside the Federal Highway Administration [par-c96cf97b739b] and the National Transportation Safety Board [par-1a25ba11ffe2]. Specific product literature values, installation instructions, creep ratings, and numerical NIST test results are not set forth in the provided claims record.
Which date does the record support?

The record better supports eve-df6e225e5c29 because its quote explicitly connects the specific report identifier and the issuing body to the date: "ESR-1531* Issued December 1, 2004 This report is subject to re-examination in one year. ICC Evaluation Service, Inc." In contrast, the quote cited by eve-0948b9a92a7e ("*Corrected January 2006 ES REPORTS™ are not to be construed as representing aesthetics...") does not reference report ESR-1531 or ICC Evaluation Service, Inc. directly within the quoted text.

The technical record documents the organizational framework, supply chain, and forensic investigation participants concerning the tunnel adhesive anchor installations. Project owner Massachusetts Highway Department (MassHighway) [par-e0ea2bb86f5c] contracted with Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) as management consultant and construction manager [par-0dd37fa6a5e7, rel-e5c16593a433, ali-94b2596ab4f6] and with Walsh Construction of Illinois for C05B1 tunnel finishes [par-aae92961cb20, rel-f7787f98dd01]. For tunnel construction, Modern Continental Construction [par-b69be329722f] had submittals reviewed by Gannett & Fleming [rel-07f6df84ed6f, par-58894ff92fb3] and retained Conam Inspection [rel-e5a39491f5d6]. Adhesive anchors were supplied by Powers Fasteners, Inc. [par-d0661af710bd, par-f629d39627a4], with adhesive formulating and manufacturing performed by Sika Corporation [par-492115b608d0, par-6a51aba71def], including Sikadur Injection Gel FS / Anchor Fix 3 - Part B [par-1d0ac17d3a67], and quality control inspections performed by CEL Consulting [par-5643a9ab141a, rel-111b103162f3, rel-c22cf0a20389]. Following the failure, forensic investigations and testing were executed by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) [par-bdf0dadf484a, par-c17d0f65c71e], the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) [par-996cb217f280, par-740d77fef13f, rel-426458740d97], and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) [par-89446cbd4d41], with additional laboratory testing contracted to Standard Testing and Engineering Company [par-3cef131a7f18, rel-490b01df5a71], Bodycote Polymer – Broutman Laboratory [par-80997c384b9e, rel-1fccab542ce0], and Trace Laboratories-East [par-38996b4e584e, rel-27a86bd58a37].

decision.summary: The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority (MTA) acted as the project authority representing the Massachusetts Highway Department (par-79fda5cf540e, rel-85d4c86b75bc). Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) served as the project management consultant and engineer overseeing general contractor Modern Continental Construction Co., Inc. (MCC) and reviewing its submittals (par-9e21da513474, par-a4dd810e276b, rel-16076210a380, rel-9e358de424fa). Powers Fasteners, Inc. supplied adhesive anchors to MCC (par-a89aefe527c8, rel-c2a0fb871269), while SIGMA Engineering provided structural calculations for MCC (rel-fdd833e79975) and Conam Inspection conducted anchor tension testing for MCC (rel-9632e76195f2). Adhesive ceiling anchorage installation and testing procedures were set by Addendum No. 12 to Specification Section 723.480 (eve-9f5aadd4ca0b). After anchor displacement was identified in the HOV ceiling mockup in September and October 1999 (eve-37835b5e0d7f, eve-83bf893053c1), B/PB directed MCC to investigate with the manufacturer and abandon or replace moving anchors (eve-21836dcf40c6). Powers Fasteners provided technical repair recommendations (eve-1d798f59998c, eve-47b2aba7e268), but B/PB rejected initial repair Submittal 723.480.016 A on November 30, 1999 (eve-9dd975510fd0) and issued Deficiency Report No. 001 (DR-001) on December 1, 1999 (eve-591f6af5d07f). MCC's subsequent repair procedure Submittal No. 723.480-016 B was submitted January 28, 2000 (eve-b440fe5603a1) and approved subject to indicated changes on February 16, 2000 (eve-468958a8d701). Following completion of re-testing and anchor replacements, B/PB closed DR-001 on January 26, 2001 (eve-b72a98d5b81e, eve-14a38b32b57b), and MTA authorized Field Work Order Modification No. 158FW for the testing work on March 14, 2001 (eve-9a0e72d0a606, eve-d6d349f81c34).

decision.summary: The technical record documents the organizational framework, supply chain, and forensic investigation participants concerning the tunnel adhesive anchor installations. Project owner Massachusetts Highway Department (MassHighway) [par-e0ea2bb86f5c] contracted with Bechtel/Parsons Brinckerhoff (B/PB) as management consultant and construction manager [par-0dd37fa6a5e7, rel-e5c16593a433, ali-94b2596ab4f6] and with Walsh Construction of Illinois for C05B1 tunnel finishes [par-aae92961cb20, rel-f7787f98dd01]. For tunnel construction, Modern Continental Construction [par-b69be329722f] had submittals reviewed by Gannett & Fleming [rel-07f6df84ed6f, par-58894ff92fb3] and retained Conam Inspection [rel-e5a39491f5d6]. Adhesive anchors were supplied by Powers Fasteners, Inc. [par-d0661af710bd, par-f629d39627a4], with adhesive formulating and manufacturing performed by Sika Corporation [par-492115b608d0, par-6a51aba71def], including Sikadur Injection Gel FS / Anchor Fix 3 - Part B [par-1d0ac17d3a67], and quality control inspections performed by CEL Consulting [par-5643a9ab141a, rel-111b103162f3, rel-c22cf0a20389]. Following the failure, forensic investigations and testing were executed by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) [par-bdf0dadf484a, par-c17d0f65c71e], the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) [par-996cb217f280, par-740d77fef13f, rel-426458740d97], and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) [par-89446cbd4d41], with additional laboratory testing contracted to Standard Testing and Engineering Company [par-3cef131a7f18, rel-490b01df5a71], Bodycote Polymer – Broutman Laboratory [par-80997c384b9e, rel-1fccab542ce0], and Trace Laboratories-East [par-38996b4e584e, rel-27a86bd58a37].

members.title: Claim professional

Your job is to get every document read by the right role or excluded with a reason, follow up open questions, rule disputes on the evidence, and close the claim file.

members.title: Defense counsel

members.job: You are the forensic engineer retained by defense counsel, with the claim professional's approval. From the records only, you set out the technical record: design requirements and values, submittals and how they were dispositioned, tests with their methods and results, deviations from requirements, repairs, and when each happened. You state documented facts, never an opinion on cause.
members.sees: as counsel, for its own documents and claims
can: as counsel, except asking for an expert
members.waits_for: expert.approved: it cannot start before the lead approves it

members.title: Readers
members.job: Read whole documents (long ones in page windows) for one role and focus; return dated events, parties, relationships, aliases and open questions, each with an exact quote.
members.sees: only their batch (about 40k characters), plus up to 2 short documents it cites by reference number
can: one automatic repair of refused claims

members.title: Dispatcher, verifier, assembly
members.mirrors: the claims system and file rules
members.job: Turns events into tasks and runs them in parallel; checks every claim against the page; tests absences; decides whether the file may close; assembles the chronology, party map and exhibits.
can: hold a task until what it waits for exists
expire stuck tasks and tell the lead
stop the run on a guard

verifier_rules: Every quote must be found on the page it cites. Whitespace, curly quotes and dashes are folded, and a word may be joined across a hyphen at a line break; case, spelling and word order must match.
A quote on a production label (a cover sheet or divider added when the claim file was assembled), or on a page outside the readable claim file, is refused.
An event dated as the document's own date must match the date read from the document; an event dated from the text must have a quote that shows that date.

A party's name must appear in its quotes, ignoring case, punctuation and corporate suffixes; a relationship's two parties must both appear. At assembly, a name also appears through a verified alias quoted in the claim.
An alias is accepted only when one quote shows both names.
A refused claim is sent back to its reader once with the page and the reason; if it still fails it is kept with its reasons, never softened.
team_spec.negative_rule: At the end, each role proposes what the claim file does not contain, with search terms that would find a counter-example. An absence is accepted only if every in-scope page was read in the run and a phrase search for each term finds nothing in scope.

memory.events: the append-only event log: every message between roles, with its cause; change streams wake consumers
memory.tasks: one task per event a role must handle: waits-for, deadline, state, outcome
memory.reservations: which task holds which document, per role (unique index), so no document is read twice by a role
memory.coverage: every page handed to a reader, with the role and focus, logged before the model runs
memory.findings / refusals: verified claims, and refused ones with the verifier's reasons
memory.exclusions: documents the lead ruled out of scope, with its reason
memory.disputes: conflicting claims on the same page and the lead's ruling
memory.model_calls: every model call: who, for which task, tokens, cost, the decision and its reasoning summary
memory.workers: every reader: documents, pages, focus, claims kept and refused
memory.checkpoints: LangGraph state of each role's task (plan, read, review, close), so a task can resume
memory.pages / documents / metadata / sources: the ingested claim file (GridFS for the PDFs, Atlas Search on page text)
memory.cache: model and parser answers, so a finished run replays for free
